title: Fabrication of flexible conductive films by rubbing in technology for application in elastic thermo-electric cells
author: Karimov, Ahmad, et al.

steps.title: Prepare strained rubber substrate
steps.instruction: Cut a commercially available rubber film (2 cm × 2 cm, thickness 80 µm). Clamp it onto a metallic round plate and stretch to a strain S = Δl/l of 1.6–1.8.

steps.title: Apply nanomaterial powder
steps.instruction: Evenly spread the desired nanomaterial or mixed nanomaterial powder onto the strained rubber surface.

steps.title: Rubbing‑in of powder
steps.instruction: Place a polished metallic load on the powder and drive it horizontally in two perpendicular directions using a mechanism set to 1–10 Hz. Apply a pressure of 5–10 g cm⁻² for 1–3 min to embed the powder into the rubber.

steps.title: Release strain and finalize film
steps.instruction: Remove the external strain to allow the rubber pores to shrink, causing the embedded nanoparticles to be squeezed. The resulting conductive film has active dimensions of 5–10 mm (length) × 5–10 mm (width) and remains electrically stable from 30–70 °C.

steps.title: Prepare measurement setup
steps.instruction: Assemble the thermo‑electric measurement rig (as shown in Fig. 3) and create a temperature difference of 5 °C across the flexible film.

steps.title: Record electrical parameters
steps.instruction: Measure the open‑circuit voltage (Voc) and calculate the Seebeck coefficient α = Voc/ΔT (ΔT = 5 °C). Optionally measure short‑circuit current (Isc) and internal resistance as described.
